reader_guide.headline: Use this page like a question map.
reader_guide.plain_answer: Start with a question. Read the plain answer. Open the source link when the concept needs evidence.
reader_guide.useful_for_reader: AI learners, founders, operators, builders, and curious people who want simple language before source links and notes.
how_to_read: Start with the question you already have.
Open AI Learning when a term is unfamiliar.
Open the note link when you want examples, numbers, limits, or visible snapshots.

website_scan.current_strength: The site already has visible routes: Articles, Field Notes, AI Learning, Proof Tour, public catalogs, benchmark numbers, limitations, heartbeat rows, and market context.
website_scan.main_question: How can a technical website explain AI systems clearly enough that a reader can understand the concept before asking for a meeting?
website_scan.reader_value: A modern AI site should behave like a guided interface: start with a question, explain the idea, show a visible route, and name the limit.
interface_principles: Use definitions and examples instead of future-plan language.
Prefer notes and public links over backend details.
Use charts, rows, and visible snapshots where numbers help the reader.
Keep the learning surface useful without exposing operational details.

modern_questions.question: How do you make an AI answer with sources instead of just sounding confident?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Teams want AI systems that can point back to the file, article, transaction, or report behind an answer.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Use retrieval augmented generation. The system searches a trusted source first, gives the model that context, then shows where the answer came from.
modern_questions.already_built_example: AI Learning explains RAG and the Proof Tour links visible routes with sources, limits, and field notes.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are checking whether an AI answer can show where it came from.

modern_questions.question: When is vector search better than keyword search?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Search gets harder when a visitor asks in different words than the article or dataset used.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Keyword search looks for exact words. Vector search looks for meaning, so it can find a relevant passage even when the wording is different.
modern_questions.already_built_example: The AI Learning Map defines embeddings and connects them to RAG, observability, and proof routes.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are comparing a normal search box with an AI search or knowledge assistant.

modern_questions.question: If you have two AI components, how do you connect them without creating a messy system?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Modern AI work often has separate parts: retrieval, tools, memory, evaluation, user interface, and approval gates.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Give each component a clear contract. One part should know what it receives, what it returns, what it is allowed to do, and what gets logged.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Proof Tour shows connected lanes for wallet risk, agent coordination, heartbeat rows, agent rules, reports, and learning concepts.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are trying to understand how small AI pieces become one usable workflow.

modern_questions.question: How do you know an AI workflow improved instead of just changed?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: A model can feel better while becoming less reliable on edge cases.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Use eval rows. Pick sample questions, expected behavior, pass or fail criteria, and notes. Then compare changes against the same set.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Field Notes shows benchmark-style values, limits, and method notes so numbers are not floating by themselves.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are reviewing AI output quality or deciding whether a change is actually better.

modern_questions.question: What should an AI agent be allowed to do by itself?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Finance, healthcare, and compliance workflows need role boundaries, approval gates, and reviewable actions.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Start with roles. Some actions can be read-only, some require review, and some should stay human-only. The log is part of the system.
modern_questions.already_built_example: AI Learning defines RBAC, audit logs, tool calling, and MCP as one rule pattern.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are thinking about AI agents in regulated or high-trust workflows.

modern_questions.question: Can a technical portfolio explain itself before the first call?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Readers, customers, and collaborators usually need a fast path from a claim to something they can inspect.
modern_questions.plain_answer: A proof route should answer four things quickly: what exists, what points to it, what the limits are, and where to click next.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Proof Tour gives a guided route through wallet risk, agent coordination, heartbeat, agent rules, reports, and modern stack signals.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you want to inspect technical work without reading the whole archive first.

modern_questions.question: How do you show AI work without exposing private systems?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Technical work needs context, but that context should not leak keys, paths, client data, infrastructure, or employer details.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Show evidence-linked artifacts: summaries, screenshots, notes, synthetic examples, public APIs, and limits. Keep the page focused on what a visitor can inspect.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Live Signals shows public heartbeat rows, market context, and snapshot limits without backend details.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you need to present technical work while protecting security and privacy.

modern_questions.question: What turns a local AI demo into something reliable enough to run again?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: A demo becomes stronger when it can be packaged, health-checked, monitored, and redeployed.
modern_questions.plain_answer: Reliability comes from repeatable setup, clear environment boundaries, health checks, logs, tests, and rollback notes.
modern_questions.already_built_example: AI Learning maps Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, observability, and system health into one reliability layer.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you are deciding whether a demo is only a clip or something that can be operated.

modern_questions.question: What makes an AI project feel like engineering, not just a blog post?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: People want methods, numbers, source links, limits, and repeatable artifacts.
modern_questions.plain_answer: A number needs context. It should say what was measured, where it came from, what it does not prove, and how someone can follow it.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Reports collects metric cards, benchmark bars, capability coverage, notes, and evidence-linked references.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you want to see whether an AI project has substance behind the writing.

modern_questions.question: What makes a website feel like an AI system instead of a static brochure?
modern_questions.why_market_asks: Modern AI websites increasingly behave like interfaces: searchable, interactive, refreshed, evidence-linked, and useful without a sales call.
modern_questions.plain_answer: The page should help someone do something: inspect, compare, learn, refresh, or follow the evidence.
modern_questions.already_built_example: Live Signals refreshes public market data in the browser and shows heartbeat rows with limits.
modern_questions.useful_for_reader: Useful if you want a website to teach, explain, and show motion without overexposing the system behind it.
